definition: A percept is the input that an intelligent agent is perceiving at any given moment.
details: It is essentially the same concept as a percept in psychology, except that it is being perceived not by the brain but by the agent. A percept is detected by a sensor, often a camera, processed accordingly, and acted upon by an actuator. Each percept is added to a "percept sequence", which is a complete history of each percept ever detected. The agent's action at any instant point may depend on the entire percept sequence up to that particular instant point. An intelligent agent chooses how to act not only based on the current percept, but the percept sequence. The next action is chosen by the agent function, which maps every percept to an action. For example, if a camera were to record a gesture, the agent would process the percepts, calculate the corresponding spatial vectors, examine its percept history, and use the agent program (the application of the agent function) to act accordingly.

explainer.lead: A percept is the single input an agent receives at one moment, detected by a sensor and acted on by an actuator. How an agent reacts can depend on its whole history of percepts, not just the current one.

tiers.eli5: Think of a driver: the road ahead right now is one percept, but what they do depends on everything they have seen since starting the car.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers feed each percept into the agent's percept sequence so the policy can condition on past observations, not just the latest frame. A common pitfall is designing for a single percept and forgetting that action choice may need the full sequence up to that instant.
tiers.paperLevel: A percept is the input an intelligent agent perceives at a given moment; percepts are detected by sensors (often cameras), processed, and acted upon by actuators, and each is appended to a percept sequence whose complete history may determine the action at any instant.

explainer.example: A camera detects an obstacle in the current frame; that percept is appended to the percept sequence, and the agent's action may depend on the full sequence up to that point.
